WHAT "RESOLVED KNOWLEDGE CONTRACT" MEANS, AND WHERE IT IS DEFINED. The registry row is one line; the definition is five places and none of them is ambiguous.

1. docs/plans/core-database-and-rls-workstream-th.md:555 -- "| 041 | resolved knowledge views/functions | Knowledge | 040 | stable query contract + tests |".
2. Same document, line 93 -- knowledge.core's cross-module read contract is `resolved_business_knowledge_v1`. That string appears EXACTLY ONCE in this repository, in that table cell, with no schema, no field, no example and no consumer.
3. Same document, line 217, the last line of §4.3's "Typed knowledge tables" -- "กฎ resolution: Industry base -> Business override -> Page override -> Content brief; hard restriction override ไม่ได้".
4. sprint-0a-industry-research-pack-th.md §4.4 "Rule precedence" -- the six-layer ladder that rule specialises, with Business policy at 4 and Page-specific facts at 5, AND the combination rule: a lower layer may add strictness and may not reduce a hard rule, an evidence requirement, privacy or consent, and a conflict must return `policy_conflict` -- "ห้ามเลือกค่าหนึ่งเงียบ ๆ", never silently pick one.
5. The DB-03 acceptance list, workstream document line 657 -- "resolved context คืนเฉพาะ Workspace/Business/Page ที่ร้องขอและมีสิทธิ์" -- and line 656, "hard restriction ถูก Page override ไม่ได้".

SO THE ORDER IS DEFINED AND THIS BATCH IS NOT REFUSING TO READ IT. What is missing is what the order operates on.

THE FOUR TERMS OF THE RULE, AND WHY THREE OF THEM ARE NOT IN THIS SCHEMA.

(a) "INDUSTRY BASE" IS NOT IN THE DATABASE. The same blueprint (§4.4 of the workstream document) puts `quality_rules`, `research_recipes`, `source_policy`, `content_templates` and `restricted_claims` on industry_pack_versions as validated JSON documents. Batch 030 created NONE of them -- its version table carries version, display_name_th, checksum and released_at -- and the industry pack contract says why that is right rather than an oversight: the pack is a bundle with "ไม่มี executable code และไม่เข้าถึง network/database โดยตรง Core Runtime เป็นผู้ load, validate, resolve และ pin version". Loading, validating, resolving and pinning are SERVER acts, and RFC-2026-021 §5 reads the same sentence and puts the resolver at 070 at the earliest.

Even the pack's IDENTITY is out of reach from batch 041, and that is a second, independent refusal: §3 of the workstream document routes every cross-module read through a named contract, and the one it names for industry.core is `resolved_industry_pack_v1`, which does not exist and belongs to A2 Industry. Nothing in 041 reads app.industry_packs, app.industry_pack_versions or app.industry_assignments, and a static test asserts it rather than trusting the header.

(b) "HARD RESTRICTION OVERRIDE ไม่ได้" NEEDS A COLUMN THAT DOES NOT EXIST. The blueprint puts hardness on `content_restrictions: level(hard|soft), category, rule, replacement guidance, jurisdiction`. Batch 040 built ONE item table typed by `kind in ('voice','audience','offers','restrictions')` -- §5's four words -- with `name` and nothing else, because §5 names no field of the family and forbids an untyped document column standing in for the rest. A knowledge item can say it IS a restriction and cannot say whether it is a HARD one, so the exception clause has no subject -- and that clause is the half of the rule that matters, because a resolution that got the ordering right and let a Page soften a hard restriction would be worse than none.

(c) "BUSINESS OVERRIDE -> PAGE OVERRIDE" HAS NO KEY TO BIND ON. An override must say WHICH row it overrides. A knowledge item carries `kind` and `name`; `name` is a display field with no uniqueness, and db/foundation/seeds/fixture-catalog.json already records why there is deliberately no `unique (business_profile_id, kind)`: "Nothing in §4, §5 or §8 says a Business holds one voice profile". So a Business may hold many `voice` items and "the Page one overrides the Business one" does not name a pair.

(d) "CONTENT BRIEF" IS BATCH 080.

AND §4.4 RULES OUT THE DEFAULT ANSWER, which is the part a reader is most likely to skip. "Override" in the ladder is NOT last-writer-wins: a lower layer may only tighten, and a conflict must be RETURNED as `policy_conflict` rather than resolved silently. A batch that implemented the obvious merge would have implemented the one behaviour the document forbids by name, and it would have looked like progress.

THE OBJECT THE REGISTRY NAMES IS ONE THIS BATCH MAY NOT CREATE. "resolved knowledge VIEWS/functions" -- a `create view` in schema app that a client reads is an ALLOWLIST ENTRY under RFC-2026-021 §3, which the decision register records as an approved decision dated 2026-09-06. An entry is five objects (a security_invoker view, a column-scoped base grant, a grant on the view, a SELECT policy on the base table, schema USAGE) plus a row in db/foundation/lint/read-allowlist.json. §3 assigns the authoring to the family owner, a countersignature to A1 Security, and the decision itself to an RFC the Product Owner rules on. §4's criterion C1 -- "a named caller exists, and it is a client" -- fails here for exactly the reason it failed for the industry catalog: there is no src/, there is no client, and the consumers any document names for resolved knowledge (research at 070, content at 080) are server-side batches that do not exist. §7/3 says the allowlist stays empty and the batch that would create a first entry is NOT YET ASSIGNED. So 041 creates no view.

WHAT IS DECIDED IS THE SCOPE HALF, AND IT IS WHAT THE BATCH BUILDS. Which rows are IN SCOPE for a request naming a Business and, optionally, a Page -- as distinct from which of them wins -- is answered four times with no contradiction: §4 invariant 3 (every knowledge row has a Business scope, the Page scope is a nullable override in the same Business); §3.3 ("policy/knowledge/asset ที่จำกัดเฉพาะเพจ"); sprint-0a-industry-research-pack-th.md:653 ("Page override/contact/footer ใช้ได้เฉพาะ target Page"); and §4.4's layer 4 sitting above layer 5 for the SAME Page, which is only meaningful if the Business layer reaches it -- which 040's own header states as "business-level knowledge reaches every Page beneath it".

So: `app.knowledge_scope_applies(item_business, item_page, in_business, in_page)`, one function, `language sql`, `immutable`, `parallel safe`, `security invoker`, EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC and granted to `authenticated` and `app_worker` and to nobody else. No view, no table, no policy, no index, no trigger, no base-table grant.

TWO CHOICES A REVIEWER SHOULD ARGUE WITH, STATED AS CHOICES.

IT PINS NO `search_path`, and every batch-021 helper does. Two reasons, and the first is the premise: the body names no table, no function, no type and no cast -- only its four parameters and the operators `=` and `is null`, which resolve from pg_catalog, implicitly first on every search path and not displaceable by a SET. There is nothing for a search_path to capture. The second is a cost: a SET clause makes a SQL function opaque to the planner's inliner, and this predicate exists to be written into a WHERE over app.knowledge_items, whose Page-scope columns §3.3 requires to be indexed and batch 040 indexed. THIS IS A DESIGN REASON AND NOT A MEASUREMENT: nothing in this increment measured a query plan and nothing claims to. The premise is asserted rather than trusted -- a test requires the body to name no schema-qualified object, so the day one appears the pin becomes required and the build says so.

`app_worker` GETS EXECUTE, and the reason is 040's property rather than symmetry. 040 grants the service SELECT on both knowledge tables and NO POLICY precisely so an empty service read is attributable to row level security rather than to a forgotten GRANT. A service that could not execute this predicate would be refused 42501 ON THE FUNCTION instead, and that attribution would hold for hand-written queries while quietly failing for every query written against the contract. `service-resolves-zero-knowledge-items` is the case that keeps it true.

THE PREDICATE IS TOTAL, AND THAT COST ONE EXTRA CONJUNCT PER NULLABLE ARGUMENT. Written the obvious way -- `item_page is null or item_page = in_page` -- it returns SQL NULL when a page-level row meets a request naming no Page. In a WHERE clause NULL filters like false, which is the right answer; in a CHECK constraint NULL passes like true, which is the opposite one. A contract that means two different things in two places is not a contract, so every conjunct that can be null carries an `is not null` beside it and the apply-time block asserts the answer is FALSE rather than merely not-true, on the exact input where the obvious version would have failed.

known_limitations: THE MERGE IS NOT BUILT, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE LIMITATION RATHER THAN A DETAIL. `resolved_business_knowledge_v1` does not exist. Batch 041 answers WHICH ROWS ARE IN SCOPE and answers nothing about which of them wins, because three of the resolution rule's four terms have no representation in the merged schema (industry rule content, a restriction's hard/soft level, and the key an override binds on) and because §4.4 forbids resolving a conflict silently. A consumer at 070 or 080 that needs a MERGED context does not have one and must not infer one from the predicate's name.

THE THREE CANDIDATE ANSWERS TO THE OVERRIDE QUESTION, recorded so the decision arrives as a choice. (A) THE PAGE LAYER REPLACES THE BUSINESS LAYER PER `kind` -- needs `unique (workspace_id, business_profile_id, page_context_profile_id, kind)`, which is a product decision that one Business has one voice, and is only compatible with §4.4 if a replacement can never soften a hard rule, which (b) below says cannot be checked. (B) THE LAYERS UNION AND CARRY THEIR RANK -- nothing is replaced, the consumer receives both rows with the layer each came from and applies §4.4 itself; needs no new key and needs a stable vocabulary for the layer, which §4.4 numbers but does not name for this schema. This is the reading closest to "ห้ามเลือกค่าหนึ่งเงียบ ๆ". (C) THE OVERRIDE IS AN EXPLICIT EDGE -- a page-level item names the business-level item it overrides, as a nullable self-referencing column; makes the pair a writer's decision rather than a resolver's inference, and costs a column and a constraint on a merged table.

NO `level(hard|soft)` ON A KNOWLEDGE ITEM, so "hard restriction override ไม่ได้" is currently unenforceable in the database and is unenforceable anywhere until the column exists. Batch 040 was right not to invent it (§5 names no field of the family) and 041 is not the batch that may.

NO ARCHIVE FILTER IN THE PREDICATE, deliberately. §11.3 says archive closes new creation while history stays readable by role; whether archived knowledge is still IN SCOPE for generation is a product question nobody has answered, and folding `archived_at is null` into a predicate named "scope" would answer it silently and in the wrong place. A caller adds the clause it wants and can see that it did -- which also means a caller that forgets it resolves archived knowledge.

THE COMMAND SURFACE GAP IS UNCHANGED AND UNPAID. Batch 040 recorded that a client holding INSERT on app.knowledge_item_versions can write a version whose `name` never was the item's, because nothing binds the two statements into one transaction. 041 is a read-side contract and binds no write path, so the gap is exactly where 040 left it.

THE `search_path` DEVIATION RESTS ON A DESIGN ARGUMENT AND NOT ON A MEASUREMENT. The claim that a SET clause would defeat SQL-function inlining, and that inlining is what keeps knowledge_items_page_scope_idx usable through the contract, is stated in the migration as a reason. No query plan was measured in this increment. A reviewer who thinks the pin should be there anyway is disagreeing with a judgement, not with a number.

A CITATION IS A CLAIM, AND ONE OF MINE WAS WRONG. It settled that the migration parses and applies, that its apply-time truth table holds against a real Postgres, that all 224 isolation cases pass, and that the negative-control delta is +4 and not +7. It also settles nothing about the query-plan claim in the search_path argument, which was a design reason on 2026-09-06 and is a design reason now.

A COMMAND SURFACE FOR knowledge.core, unchanged from batch 040's recommendation and not paid here. A client holding INSERT on app.knowledge_item_versions can write a version whose `name` never was the item's; RLS cannot fix a property of a write path.

BATCH 070 (research), which §6 makes depend on 030, 040, 050 and 061, and which is the first declared consumer of resolved knowledge. It inherits app.knowledge_scope_applies as the scope filter rather than writing the two-branch condition inline -- which is the drift the function exists to prevent -- and it inherits the merge as an open decision rather than as a gap it may fill by default.

THEN DECIDE WHETHER THE REFUSAL TO MERGE IS RIGHT. The argument is that three of the rule's four terms are absent from the schema and that §4.4 forbids the obvious default. The strongest case AGAINST it is that reading (B) -- union the layers and let the consumer apply §4.4 -- needs no new key and no new column, so 041 could have returned both layers with a rank and left the conflict to the caller. I did not, because §4.4 numbers Business 4 and Page 5 with layer 5 labelled "Page-specific facts/footer/contact", and a page-level `restrictions` item is not a fact, a footer or a contact -- mapping 040's rows onto that numbering is an interpretation, and an interpretation encoded as an integer is the hardest kind to argue with later. If you think that is too cautious, the change is a `layer` or `rank` output on a set-returning function, and it needs the RFC either way.

THEN READ THE `search_path` DEVIATION, which is the one place this batch departs from batch 021's helper shape. Two claims hold it up: the body names no object (asserted by a test, so it cannot quietly stop being true), and a SET clause would defeat inlining (a design reason, NOT measured here). If you think the pin belongs there anyway, say so -- the cost is an optimisation barrier on a predicate meant for a WHERE clause, and that cost is a judgement rather than a fact I measured.

THEN CHECK THAT THE TWO KINDS OF NEGATIVE ARE NOT CONFLATED. Three of the fifteen new cases are refused by the PREDICATE and would return nothing with row level security switched off; four are refused by row level security while the predicate ADMITS the row. Only the second group belongs to the CI negative control, and .github/workflows/ci.yml says so explicitly. A reviewer's best attack here is to check that each predicate negative really is paired with a case differing in exactly ONE argument -- the test 'every predicate negative is paired with a statement that differs in exactly one argument' asserts it by identity, by row and by request, and probe P12 (re-pointing a negative at the passing request) is the reversal it refuses.

THE PROBE ROUND'S FINDING IS ABOUT THE TESTS AND IS WORTH READING FOR ITS SHAPE. The totality guard compared the expected constant against itself and would have passed against a migration with no function in it; it also meant three independent reversals were all caught by ONE assertion. That is batch 040's USING/WITH-CHECK scar in a new shape, and the general rule it suggests -- an assertion over a whole expression is one deletion away from covering nothing -- is worth applying to the other suites in this package.
